thesis: Aggressive tier, but the book is 85% cash at the opening tick, so the dominant risk today is under-deployment rather than drawdown. Regime context supports adding beta: VIX 15.81 (-1.62%) is calm, WTI -2.43% and USO -3.01% ease the fuel/inflation drag that dominated the mid-September lessons, 10Y ticked down to 5.226%, and the 2026-09-28 US-China agreement on ~$60bn of tariff cuts removes a small tail risk even though rare earths are unresolved. Single-name news in this pack is mostly noise (SPAC/biotech 8-Ks, Reg FD filings); the two decision-relevant items are TSMC reportedly scouting a second US fab hub and continued sell-side framing of semis (Nvidia valuation, Micron as an S&P profit driver) — a capex/supply theme, not a tradable single-name catalyst, so I express it through SMH rather than a single chip name. I add VTI as the core because it is the one line the book already owns and the one that cleared consensus yesterday. Sizing stays inside shared caps: post-fill VTI ~$300 (30% of ~$1000 sizing equity, under the 35% name cap), SMH ~$100 (10%), cash ~$600 (60%, far above the 15% floor), 2 of 6 positions used. I deliberately leave room to press later in the session rather than max out on the first bucket, since 09:30 prints are the least informative of the day. Noted risk I accept: SMH carries Micron exposure into an earnings event the pack flags as upcoming, and 10Y above 5% keeps multiple compression live. Prices/levels cited are only those in the signals block; I make no assumption about this tick's fills.
